# Game of 24 reference rules

A puzzle consists of four integer cards. Use each card exactly once. Repeated
card values represent separate cards. Combine them using addition, subtraction,
multiplication, division, and parentheses to obtain exactly 24. Concatenation,
exponentiation, factorials, extra constants, and executable code are prohibited.

Fractional and negative intermediate values are permitted. Division by zero is
never permitted. Preserve rational values exactly rather than rounding decimals.
An intermediate value of 24 is not sufficient if unused cards remain.

Useful strategies include grouping pairs, forming a useful difference, and
retaining a fractional intermediate when integer-only choices fail. Compare
candidate expressions, then submit the best candidate to an independent exact
verifier. Evaluator confidence is not mathematical proof. If verification fails,
use its concrete feedback to revise the proposal within the supervisor's budget.

# Game of 24: Agentic Reasoning Reference Notes
This is local course reference material, not a benchmark answer key. It contains rules, definitions, and general methods only. It deliberately omits worked answers to the five evaluation cases.

## A. Objective and card identity
The input is a multiset of exactly four card values. Every physical card must be used exactly once even when two or more cards have the same face value. The goal is a fully parenthesized arithmetic expression whose value equals exactly twenty-four. A partial expression that reaches twenty-four before consuming the remaining cards is not a solution. Check the complete expression's leaf constants against the original multiset, not merely the numerical final result. A trustworthy verifier reports both the evaluated value and the number-use check separately.

## B. Allowed syntax and arithmetic
Only addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, integer card literals and grouping parentheses belong to the basic Game-of-24 language. Card concatenation, power, roots, factorial, invented constants, variable names, Python calls, attribute access and executable text are outside the allowed language. Division by zero is illegal, including division by a computed intermediate zero. Subtraction may produce a negative intermediate value.
